questions.q: Intensive distribution means a product is:
o: sold in as many outlets as possible
sold in only one store per region
questions.x: Convenience goods like gum use intensive distribution.

questions.q: How does retailing differ from marketing?
o: Marketing is only advertising, while retailing is everything else
Retailing is one part of marketing focused on selling to final consumers
questions.x: Marketing covers all activities that move products from producer to consumer; retailing is the final step.

questions.q: Retailers use customer databases to:
o: analyze buying patterns and plan products and promotions
questions.x: Data from loyalty programs and POS reveal what customers buy.

questions.q: Self-checkout kiosks are an example of how technology affects retailing by:
o: reducing wait times and labor costs
questions.x: Technology changes how customers shop and how stores operate.

questions.q: A retailer that sells a wide variety of products at low prices with minimal service, such as a warehouse club, is called a:
questions.x: Discounters compete on price and volume.

questions.q: A channel of distribution is:
o: a television channel used for ads
the path a product takes from the producer to the final user
questions.x: Channels may include wholesalers, distributors, and retailers.

questions.q: A wholesaler typically:
o: buys large quantities from producers and sells to retailers
questions.x: Wholesalers are intermediaries between producers and retailers.

questions.q: Omnichannel retailing means:
o: providing a seamless shopping experience across stores, websites, apps, and social media
questions.x: Customers can browse online, buy in store, and return through any channel.

questions.q: Exclusive distribution means:
o: a product is sold through a very limited number of outlets in a market
a product is sold only by wholesalers
questions.x: Luxury brands often use exclusive distribution.

questions.q: A point-of-sale (POS) system helps retailers by:
o: processing sales and recording data about items sold and inventory
questions.x: POS data supports inventory and buying decisions.

questions.q: Which technology lets shoppers buy online and pick up the order in the store?
o: BOPIS (buy online, pick up in store)
questions.x: BOPIS combines e-commerce convenience with physical stores.

questions.q: Retailing is defined as:
o: selling goods and services directly to final consumers for personal use
selling goods only to other businesses
questions.x: Retailers are the last link in the channel of distribution.

questions.q: Which is the final step of the selling process?
questions.x: Follow-up comes after closing.

questions.q: Which closing technique offers the customer a choice between two options, both of which result in a sale?
questions.x: 'Would you like the 32-inch or the 40-inch?'

questions.q: Monitoring on-floor selling activities allows managers to:
o: coach employees and improve customer service
questions.x: Observation and sales data guide coaching.

questions.q: A sales receipt is important retail sales documentation because it:
o: sets the price of future items
is required only for cash sales
replaces the product warranty in every case
provides proof of purchase for returns and records the transaction
questions.x: Accurate documentation supports returns, warranties, and accounting.

questions.q: Cross-selling in retail means:
o: selling complementary products from other categories
questions.x: Example: selling a phone case with a phone.

questions.q: A sales quota is:
o: a sales goal assigned to an employee or department for a period
questions.x: Quotas measure sales performance.

questions.q: Demonstrating a product during a sale helps by:
o: showing the customer how the product's features meet their needs
questions.x: Demonstrations involve the senses and build confidence.

questions.q: Suggestion selling is:
o: recommending additional items related to a customer's purchase
pressuring customers to buy expensive items
questions.x: Example: suggesting batteries with a toy purchase.

questions.q: A merchandise approach to a retail customer involves:
o: opening the conversation with a comment about the product the customer is looking at
questions.x: It shows interest in what the customer is examining.

questions.q: A customer returns an item with a receipt within the return period. The salesperson should:
o: process the return according to store policy courteously
give store credit only for cash purchases always
questions.x: Following policy maintains goodwill.

questions.q: The approach step of a retail sale is when the salesperson:
o: first greets and makes contact with the customer
questions.x: Approaches include greeting, service, and merchandise approaches.

questions.q: Recommending a higher-priced, higher-quality version of a product is called:
questions.x: Upselling moves a customer to a better model.

questions.q: Informing sales staff about incoming merchandise helps them:
o: answer customer questions and promote new products
questions.x: Product knowledge improves selling.

questions.q: The standing-room-only close encourages a customer to buy by:
o: pointing out that the product or price may not be available later
questions.x: It creates urgency, which must be honest.

questions.q: When a customer says, 'This is too expensive,' the salesperson should:
o: immediately cut the price in half
explain the product's value and benefits that justify the price
questions.x: Objections can be turned into selling points by emphasizing value.

questions.q: Features differ from benefits because benefits:
o: are the physical characteristics of the product
describe how the product helps the customer
questions.x: A feature is 'waterproof'; the benefit is 'stays dry in the rain.'

questions.q: A layaway transaction allows a customer to:
o: reserve merchandise by making payments until it is paid in full
questions.x: Retailers hold the merchandise until the final payment.

questions.q: Handling a customer who is 'just looking' is best done by:
o: giving them space while letting them know you are available
questions.x: Respecting customers builds comfort and trust.

questions.q: A trial close is used to:
o: test whether the customer is ready to buy
questions.x: Example: 'Would you prefer it in blue or black?'

questions.q: Determining customer needs is best done by:
o: asking open-ended questions and listening carefully
questions.x: Questioning and listening uncover wants and needs.

questions.q: Commission pay for retail salespeople is based on:
o: a percentage of the sales they make
questions.x: Commissions reward sales performance.

questions.q: After-sale follow-up helps retailers:
o: build customer loyalty and repeat business
questions.x: Thank-you notes and service calls strengthen relationships.

questions.q: A sales transaction where the customer pays with a credit card is processed by:
o: authorizing the card through the POS system
questions.x: Electronic authorization verifies available credit.

questions.q: Converting an objection into a selling point is called the:
questions.x: The salesperson turns the objection into a reason to buy.

questions.q: Return on investment (ROI) is calculated as:
o: (gain from investment − cost of investment) ÷ cost of investment
questions.x: ROI measures profitability relative to cost.

questions.q: A retailer buys a shirt for $20 and marks it up 50% based on cost. What is the selling price?
A markdown is:
o: a reduction from the original selling price
questions.x: Markdowns clear slow-moving or seasonal merchandise.

questions.q: A store has fixed costs of $12,000, sells an item for $25, and has a variable cost of $15 per unit. What is the break-even point?
Price lining means:
o: offering merchandise at a few set price points, such as good, better, and best
questions.x: Price lines simplify customer choice.

questions.q: Cost-based pricing sets prices by:
o: adding a markup to the cost of the product
asking customers what they will pay
questions.x: Cost-plus pricing ensures costs are covered.

questions.q: Psychological pricing, such as $9.99 instead of $10.00, is based on:
o: the perception that the price is noticeably lower
questions.x: Odd pricing makes prices seem lower.

questions.q: An item costs $30 and sells for $50. What is the markup percentage based on retail (selling) price?
Keystone pricing means:
o: doubling the cost of an item to set its retail price
setting a price that ends in 9
questions.x: A $15 item becomes $30.

questions.q: Break-even point in units equals:
o: fixed costs ÷ (selling price − variable cost per unit)
questions.x: Each unit contributes (price − variable cost) toward fixed costs.

questions.q: Demand-based pricing sets prices according to:
o: what customers are willing to pay
questions.x: Prices rise when demand is strong.

questions.q: Competition-based pricing means:
o: setting prices relative to competitors' prices
questions.x: Retailers may price above, at, or below competitors.

questions.q: Demographic information includes:
questions.x: Demographics are measurable population characteristics.

questions.q: A target customer profile describes:
o: the demographic, psychographic, and behavioral traits of the customers a store wants to serve
questions.x: Profiles guide merchandise and promotion decisions.

questions.q: Market research helps retailers determine market needs by:
o: gathering information from surveys, sales data, and observation
questions.x: Research reduces risk in merchandising decisions.

questions.q: Focus groups are used in retail research to:
o: gather in-depth opinions from a small group of customers
questions.x: Focus groups provide qualitative insights.

questions.q: Geographic segmentation divides customers by:
o: location, such as region, city, or climate
questions.x: A store may stock snow boots in northern locations.

questions.q: A marketing plan for a retail store typically includes:
o: target market, goals, strategies, budget, and evaluation
questions.x: The plan guides marketing decisions for a set period.

questions.q: Psychographic information includes a customer's:
questions.x: Psychographics explain why customers buy.

questions.q: A SWOT analysis examines a retailer's:
questions.x: SWOT supports strategic market planning.

questions.q: Customer demand for merchandise can be estimated using:
o: past sales data, trends, and seasonal patterns
questions.x: Forecasting uses history and trends.

questions.q: Trend analysis helps retailers by:
o: identifying products likely to grow in popularity
questions.x: Spotting trends early drives buying decisions.

questions.q: Market segmentation means:
o: selling to everyone the same way
dividing a market into groups of customers with similar needs
questions.x: Segmentation lets retailers target specific groups.

questions.q: A retailer that targets environmentally conscious shoppers is segmenting by:
questions.x: Values and lifestyle are psychographic factors.

questions.q: A bill of lading is:
o: a document listing goods shipped and the terms of shipment
questions.x: It serves as a contract between shipper and carrier.

questions.q: Which mode of transportation is usually the fastest for long distances but most expensive?
questions.x: Air is fast but costly; it suits urgent or high-value items.

questions.q: Planning storage space in a stockroom involves:
o: organizing merchandise so it is easy to find, protected, and rotated
questions.x: Good layout speeds restocking and reduces damage.

questions.q: When selecting a shipping method, a retailer considers:
o: cost, speed, product characteristics, and reliability
only the color of the truck
questions.x: Perishable or high-value goods may justify faster, costlier shipping.

questions.q: FIFO stock rotation means:
o: the newest items are sold first
first in, first out — older stock is sold before newer stock
questions.x: FIFO is critical for perishable goods.

questions.q: A distribution center differs from a traditional warehouse because it:
o: focuses on moving goods quickly to stores rather than long-term storage
questions.x: DCs emphasize throughput and fast fulfillment.

questions.q: A perpetual inventory system:
o: continuously updates inventory records with each sale and receipt
counts inventory only once a year
questions.x: POS systems enable perpetual inventory.

questions.q: A periodic inventory system:
o: determines inventory by physical counts at set intervals
questions.x: Counts may be monthly, quarterly, or annually.

questions.q: Safety stock is:
o: extra inventory kept to prevent stockouts
questions.x: It buffers against unexpected demand or delays.

questions.q: Inventory shrinkage is:
o: loss of inventory from theft, damage, or errors
questions.x: Shrinkage = recorded inventory − actual inventory.

questions.q: Cycle counting is a method of:
o: counting a small portion of inventory on a rotating schedule
questions.x: Regular cycle counts catch errors without shutting down.

questions.q: Electronic article surveillance (EAS) tags are used to:
o: deter shoplifting by triggering alarms at exits
questions.x: EAS reduces theft-related shrinkage.

questions.q: The reorder point is the inventory level at which:
o: a new order should be placed
questions.x: It accounts for lead time and safety stock.

questions.q: Stockturn (inventory turnover) measures:
o: how many times inventory is sold and replaced during a period
questions.x: Turnover = net sales ÷ average inventory at retail (or cost of goods sold ÷ average inventory at cost).

questions.q: Allocating merchandise to stores means:
o: deciding how much of each product each store or region receives
questions.x: Allocation considers each location's sales and demand.

questions.q: Which is the largest common source of retail shrinkage?
questions.x: Theft is the leading cause, followed by administrative errors and damage.

questions.q: A stockout occurs when:
o: a store has too much inventory
a product is out of stock and unavailable to customers
questions.x: Stockouts lead to lost sales and unhappy customers.

questions.q: Unit inventory control tracks:
o: only the dollar value of stock
the number of individual units of merchandise
questions.x: Unit control helps with reordering specific items.

questions.q: Dollar inventory control tracks:
o: the number of units of each SKU only
questions.x: Dollar control supports budgeting and open-to-buy.

questions.q: A stock-keeping unit (SKU) is:
o: a unique code identifying a specific product, including size and color
questions.x: SKUs track items at a detailed level.

questions.q: Tracking stock by location, department, class, and vendor helps buyers:
o: identify what sells where and from which supplier
questions.x: Detailed tracking supports better buying decisions.

questions.q: Records show $50,000 of inventory, but a physical count finds $48,500. What is the shrinkage?
RFID tags help retailers by:
o: tracking inventory automatically using radio signals
questions.x: RFID speeds counts and improves accuracy.

questions.q: An on-floor assortment refers to:
o: the selection of merchandise displayed on the sales floor
questions.x: It balances variety with available space.

questions.q: Visual merchandising is:
o: only the store's advertising on TV
the coordination of all physical elements in a store to attract customers and encourage sales
questions.x: It includes layout, displays, signage, and lighting.

questions.q: A free-form layout is commonly used in:
questions.x: Free-form layouts encourage browsing.

questions.q: Impulse items, such as candy and magazines, are often placed:
o: at the back of the store
questions.x: Customers make last-minute purchases while waiting.

questions.q: Lighting in visual merchandising is used to:
o: highlight merchandise and create a mood
questions.x: Accent lighting draws attention to key displays.

questions.q: Placing high-demand items at the back of a grocery store encourages customers to:
questions.x: Customers see more products on the way.

questions.q: A planogram is:
o: a diagram showing where each product should be placed on shelves and fixtures
questions.x: Planograms ensure consistent, strategic placement.

questions.q: A grid store layout is commonly used in:
o: grocery and drug stores with long parallel aisles
questions.x: Grid layouts are efficient for routine shopping.

questions.q: Cross-merchandising means:
o: displaying related items from different departments together
questions.x: Example: pasta displayed with sauce and parmesan.

questions.q: Eye-level shelf space is considered the most valuable because:
o: products there are most likely to be noticed and purchased
questions.x: 'Eye level is buy level.'

questions.q: The 'decompression zone' of a store is:
o: the area just inside the entrance where customers adjust to the store
questions.x: Important merchandise is usually placed just beyond it.

questions.q: Signage helps customers by:
questions.x: Clear signs improve navigation and sales.

questions.q: The pyramid arrangement in a display:
o: keeps all items at the same height
builds merchandise up to a high point at the center
questions.x: Pyramids create a triangle that leads the eye upward.

questions.q: A point-of-purchase (POP) display is placed:
o: where customers make buying decisions, such as near the register
questions.x: POP displays encourage impulse purchases.

questions.q: An asymmetrical display:
o: balances items of different sizes and shapes for a more casual look
questions.x: Informal balance uses visual weight rather than mirror images.

questions.q: The focal point of a display is:
o: the area that first attracts the viewer's attention
questions.x: Every effective display has a clear focal point.

questions.q: Changing displays regularly helps because:
o: it keeps the store fresh and encourages repeat visits
questions.x: New displays give customers reasons to look again.

questions.q: A window display is primarily intended to:
questions.x: Windows create a first impression.

questions.q: Which display arrangement creates a formal look with equal weight on both sides?
questions.x: Formal balance mirrors items on each side.

questions.q: A mannequin is an example of a display:
questions.x: Forms show how clothing looks when worn.

questions.q: A gondola is a:
o: freestanding fixture with shelves on both sides
questions.x: Gondolas are common in grocery and discount stores.

questions.q: Promotional signs should be:
o: clear, brief, and easy to read from a distance
crowded with as much text as possible
questions.x: Effective signs communicate quickly.

questions.q: Display fixtures should be selected based on:
o: the merchandise type, store image, and available space
questions.x: Fixtures must showcase products and fit the store's brand.

questions.q: An endcap display is located:
o: at the end of an aisle
questions.x: Endcaps have high visibility and are used for promotions.

questions.q: A convenience store typically has an assortment that is:
questions.x: It carries many categories with few choices in each.

questions.q: Selecting the quality of merchandise to offer should be based mainly on:
o: the target customers' expectations and the store's image
questions.x: Quality must fit the target market and price points.

questions.q: A product mix is:
o: all of the products a retailer offers for sale
questions.x: It is described by width, depth, and consistency.

questions.q: A national brand is:
o: a brand owned by one store
a brand owned by a manufacturer and sold through many retailers
questions.x: National brands carry strong recognition.

questions.q: A private-label (store) brand is:
o: an unbranded generic item from a farm
a brand owned by the manufacturer and sold everywhere
a brand owned and sold by the retailer
questions.x: Store brands often offer higher margins.

questions.q: The depth of an assortment refers to:
o: the number of choices (styles, sizes, colors) within each product line
questions.x: A specialty shoe store has a deep assortment.

questions.q: The width (breadth) of an assortment refers to:
o: the number of different product lines carried
the number of items within one line
questions.x: A department store has a wide assortment.

questions.q: Open-to-buy is:
o: the amount a buyer has available to purchase merchandise for a period
questions.x: It helps prevent overbuying.

questions.q: Planning a merchandise assortment includes deciding:
questions.x: Assortment planning matches customer demand.

questions.q: Product line extension in a retail assortment means:
o: adding new items to an existing product line
questions.x: Example: adding new flavors or sizes.

questions.q: A specialty store typically has an assortment that is:
questions.x: Specialty retailers focus on a few lines with many choices.

questions.q: A brand mix that includes both national and private-label brands helps a retailer:
o: appeal to different customers while improving margins
questions.x: National brands draw traffic; store brands boost profit.
